Approving: the person approves on the first-party page GET /api/_mcp/operations/{id} by POST /api/_mcp/operations/{id}/approve with a CSRF token bound to that session and that one operation (the unbound /api/_csrf token and a token for another operation are refused) from a direct, unscoped, non-impersonated, non-act-as cookie session of the same user, account incarnation and workspace. Any Authorization header, connector credential, API token or bearer session is refused, and the link itself grants nothing. There is no approve tool. A repeated approval answers 409.

Who sees the page: unknown, foreign and refused operations answer with one identical styled 404 page ("This request can't be shown"); a signed-out request to a review or batch link is redirected to /login?next= first. An infrastructure failure answers 503 on the review page.

Review page content: the page shows the title and summary; the model-facing description appears (collapsed under "What the assistant was told") only for a tool that declares neither. It shows one labelled row per preview key (a humanised key when no label is declared; strings as written, Yes/No, a dash for null, nested values as compact JSON, invisible characters shown as \u escapes), and under "Exact data" the stored preview as indented JSON in which every invisible, bidi-control, format, control or non-ASCII space character is written as its JSON \u escape (nothing else is escaped, so & < > read as written; the page HTML-escapes the text); it wraps long values. It lists each delivery the command can queue (the hook actions and matching webhook subscriptions on its write tables) before approval, under disclosure version v2; SQL hook writes are not itemized. Its CSP admits only its own hashed style. Which state the page shows is in `review_page_state` (1).

Review text: a command tool in mcp.yaml may declare `title` (at most 80 characters, e.g. Create a project), `review_summary` (at most 500, one or two sentences for the person approving), `labels: {<key>: Country}` (at most 60 characters each; a key names an intent argument property, a preview key or, with a field-driven `review_changes` entry, an enum value of that field) and `review_changes: [{before: old_value, after: new_value, field: field}]` for an app whose prepare returns a flat preview (`field` names the preview key holding the changed field, or use `label: Role` for a fixed row label; before, after and field must be string-typed preview_schema properties). No control, invisible or direction-changing character is accepted; these fields are reviewed content in the contract digest, and a manifest that declares none keeps its digest.

Before and after: a before value is shown only when the command's own prepare step read it on the server and returned it in the preview: either a flat pair named by `review_changes` or a preview property that preview_schema declares as an object with exactly `before` and `after`. The operation digest seals it and it is never re-read at review time, and a nested object the schema does not declare that way is never treated as a pair. Every other preview key is context: on a page with before/after rows it shows its value across both columns, never an "(empty)" before, while a pair whose before was read as empty still shows Before "(empty)" and keeps the Before column. Native `table.update` tools are not prepared or reviewed and have no before/after.

Batch approval: prepared results also carry batch_review_url (/api/_mcp/operations/batch?grant=<id>): one page listing every pending, unexpired operation that grant prepared for the signed-in person (those that can no longer be applied are listed apart, see `review_page_state` (1)), with the single-operation page's gates (cookie session only, direct login, rate limits with every approval charged as it is approved, CSP), no operation ticked by default, and one CSRF token bound to the session and grant:<id>. Its POST approves each selected operation through the same review path in its own transaction, so each stays a human approval.

Auto-approve: grant-consented auto-approval is opt-in and needs all three of these. (1) The reviewed manifest declares approval: grant on the command tool (command tools only; table.update and transfer tools, which push app data to an external connection, stay first_party and grant is refused on them). (2) The owner runs `benmore mcp enable <app> --writes --auto-approve` (refused when no command declares approval: grant); `benmore mcp disable <app> --auto-approve` turns only it off, and every path that rotates the write epoch, including disable --writes, a full disable, revoke and restore, ends it. (3) The user ticks the unticked consent checkbox listing the live approval: grant commands within the connection's scopes, offered only while the switch is on; the form can only accept or decline that list, and it can only shrink afterwards (refresh never changes it).

Auto-approve validity: the consent is honoured only while the owner has not switched auto-approve off and on since the user consented and the tool's entry still matches the current manifest contract digest. An owner off/on cycle, any write-epoch rotation or an mcp.yaml change sends the connection back to per-write review until the user reconnects. While it holds, a command call prepares, records the approval (basis grant_consent:<grant id>, approver = the actor) and commits in one call, audits mcp_command_approve with that basis, and returns the _commit shape {operation_id, outcome, receipt}; a failure returns the error with _meta.operation_id for _status/_commit reconciliation. Every commit re-checks the approval: the caller's grant, the current declaration still approval: grant, the switch still on as it was at consent, and the tool still in the grant's list, on top of the grant, credential, account, roles-intersected scopes, expiry and digests, so revoke, disable --auto-approve, a re-enable, a manifest change back to first_party, a role downgrade or disable --writes stops even a retried _commit. Receipts report approval_basis: human or grant_consent:<grant id>.

Approval reason: a prepared connector call also returns `approval_reason`, the fixed phrase for why it was not applied automatically: This kind of change always needs your approval (the tool is not `approval: grant`), Auto-approve is turned off for this app, This connection was not allowed to auto-approve <title or tool name>, The app's tools changed since you connected; reconnect the assistant to re-enable auto-approve, or Auto-approve was switched off and on since you connected; reconnect to re-enable it. The same phrase is stored with the operation and shown on the review page; `_commit` still re-checks all three opt-ins.

Rate limits: the review and approve routes are rate limited: a coarse per-IP flood guard before authentication (120/minute), a per-user approval budget (30/minute) and a separate per-user review budget (120/minute), both charged only for a real operation the caller prepared (never for unknown ids or a cross-site navigation), so neither an anonymous caller on a shared address nor a hostile page can spend a person's approvals; both answer 429 with Retry-After.
